component.name: rocketmq
component.title: RocketMQ
component.description: Send messages to and receive messages from Apache RocketMQ topics.
component.label: messaging

accessChannel.label: common
accessChannel.description: The access channel of the RocketMQ client: LOCAL for an Apache RocketMQ cluster, or CLOUD for a RocketMQ service of a cloud provider. With CLOUD the message traces go to a trace topic per region, in the format of the cloud service.

enableTrace.label: common
enableTrace.description: Whether the producer and the consumer record message traces, which the RocketMQ client sends to the trace topic RMQ_SYS_TRACE_TOPIC. The consumer of replyToTopic does not record traces.

namespace.label: common
namespace.description: The namespace of the topics and groups, which the RocketMQ client sends with each request. Set it for a RocketMQ instance that uses namespaces, such as a serverless instance. The consumer of replyToTopic does not use it.

namesrvAddr.label: common
namesrvAddr.description: The address of the RocketMQ name server, as host:port. Separate several name servers with a semicolon.

sendTag.label: common
sendTag.description: The tag of each message that the producer sends. The CamelRocketMQOverrideTag header replaces it. If not set, the messages are sent with an empty tag.

bridgeErrorHandler.label: consumer
bridgeErrorHandler.description: Allows for bridging the consumer to the Camel routing Error Handler, which mean any exceptions (if possible) occurred while the Camel consumer is trying to pickup incoming messages, or the likes, will now be processed as a message and handled by the routing Error Handler. Important: This is only possible if the 3rd party component allows Camel to be alerted if an exception was thrown. Some components handle this internally only, and therefore bridgeErrorHandler is not possible. In other situations we may improve the Camel component to hook into the 3rd party component and make this possible for future releases. By default the consumer will use the org.apache.camel.spi.ExceptionHandler to deal with exceptions, that will be logged at WARN or ERROR level and ignored.

consumerGroup.label: consumer
consumerGroup.description: The consumer group of the consumer. The consumers of a group share the messages of the topic, and each message goes to one of them. The consumer fails to start if it is not set.

messageSelectorType.label: consumer
messageSelectorType.description: How the consumer selects the messages of the topic that it receives: tag uses the subscribeTags option, and sql uses the subscribeSql option.

subscribeSql.label: consumer
subscribeSql.description: The SQL92 expression on the message properties that selects the messages that the consumer receives, when messageSelectorType is sql. The broker must have enablePropertyFilter set to true. The default 1 = 1 receives all messages.

subscribeTags.label: consumer
subscribeTags.description: The tags of the messages that the consumer receives, when messageSelectorType is tag. Separate several tags with ||, for example TagA||TagB. The default * receives all messages.

lazyStartProducer.label: producer
lazyStartProducer.description: Whether the producer should be started lazy (on the first message). By starting lazy you can use this to allow CamelContext and routes to startup in situations where a producer may otherwise fail during starting and cause the route to fail being started. By deferring this startup to be lazy then the startup failure can be handled during routing messages via Camel's routing error handlers. Beware that when the first message is processed then creating and starting the producer may take a little time and prolong the total processing time of the processing.

producerGroup.label: producer
producerGroup.description: The producer group of the producer. The producer fails to start if it is not set.

replyToConsumerGroup.label: producer
replyToConsumerGroup.description: The consumer group that receives the replies on replyToTopic, required with replyToTopic. Use a group per producer: in a shared group a reply can reach another producer, which ignores it, and the exchange times out.

replyToTopic.label: producer
replyToTopic.description: The topic on which the producer receives the reply of an InOut exchange. The reply must carry the keys of the request, one of which the producer generates to match the reply. If not set, an InOut exchange does not wait for a reply.

waitForSendResult.label: producer
waitForSendResult.description: Whether the producer waits for the send result before the exchange continues. When true, a send that fails, or whose status is not SEND_OK, fails the exchange. When false, an InOnly exchange continues as soon as the message is handed to the RocketMQ client, and a failed send is only logged. An InOut exchange always waits for the send result, and for the reply when replyToTopic is set.

autowiredEnabled.label: advanced
autowiredEnabled.description: Whether autowiring is enabled. This is used for automatic autowiring options (the option must be marked as autowired) by looking up in the registry to find if there is a single instance of matching type, which then gets configured on the component. This can be used for automatic configuring JDBC data sources, JMS connection factories, AWS Clients, etc.

requestTimeoutCheckerIntervalMillis.label: advanced
requestTimeoutCheckerIntervalMillis.description: How often, in milliseconds, the producer checks for InOut exchanges whose requestTimeoutMillis has passed. A timeout can be detected up to this interval late.

requestTimeoutMillis.label: advanced
requestTimeoutMillis.description: How long, in milliseconds, the producer waits for the reply of an InOut exchange on replyToTopic before it fails the exchange with an ExchangeTimedOutException. A value of 0 or less waits for Integer.MAX_VALUE milliseconds (about 24 days).

accessKey.label: secret
accessKey.description: The access key of the RocketMQ ACL credentials. The producer and the consumer sign their requests only when both accessKey and secretKey are set. The consumer of replyToTopic does not use it.

secretKey.label: secret
secretKey.description: The secret key of the RocketMQ ACL credentials. The producer and the consumer sign their requests only when both accessKey and secretKey are set. The consumer of replyToTopic does not use it.

CamelRocketMQTopic.label: consumer
CamelRocketMQTopic.description: The topic of the message. The consumer sets it, and so does the producer for the reply of an InOut exchange.

CamelRocketMQTag.label: consumer
CamelRocketMQTag.description: The tag of the message, or null if it has none.

CamelRocketMQKey.label: consumer
CamelRocketMQKey.description: The keys of the message, separated by a space if there are several, or null if it has none.

CamelRocketMQOverrideTopicName.label: producer
CamelRocketMQOverrideTopicName.description: The topic to send the message to. It replaces the topic name of the endpoint.

CamelRocketMQOverrideTag.label: producer
CamelRocketMQOverrideTag.description: The tag of the message to send. It replaces the sendTag option.

CamelRocketMQOverrideMessageKey.label: producer
CamelRocketMQOverrideMessageKey.description: The keys of the message to send, separated by a space if there are several. For an InOut exchange the producer adds a key that it generates to match the reply.

CamelRocketMQBrokerName.label: consumer
CamelRocketMQBrokerName.description: The name of the broker that holds the message queue of the message.

CamelRocketMQQueueId.label: consumer
CamelRocketMQQueueId.description: The ID of the message queue of the topic that holds the message.

CamelRocketMQStoreSize.label: consumer
CamelRocketMQStoreSize.description: The size in bytes of the message as the broker stored it.

CamelRocketMQQueueOffset.label: consumer
CamelRocketMQQueueOffset.description: The offset of the message in its message queue.

CamelRocketMQSysFlag.label: consumer
CamelRocketMQSysFlag.description: The system flags of the message, a bit set that RocketMQ uses for compression and the transaction type.

CamelRocketMQBornTimestamp.label: consumer
CamelRocketMQBornTimestamp.description: The time when the producer sent the message, in milliseconds since the epoch.

CamelRocketMQBornHost.label: consumer
CamelRocketMQBornHost.description: The address of the producer client that sent the message.

CamelRocketMQStoreTimestamp.label: consumer
CamelRocketMQStoreTimestamp.description: The time when the broker stored the message, in milliseconds since the epoch.

CamelRocketMQStoreHost.label: consumer
CamelRocketMQStoreHost.description: The address of the broker that stored the message.

CamelRocketMQMsgId.label: consumer
CamelRocketMQMsgId.description: The ID of the message: the unique ID that the producer client created for it, or else the offset message ID that the broker built from its address and the commit log offset.

CamelRocketMQCommitLogOffset.label: consumer
CamelRocketMQCommitLogOffset.description: The physical offset of the message in the commit log of the broker.

CamelRocketMQBodyCrc.label: consumer
CamelRocketMQBodyCrc.description: The CRC32 checksum of the message body, which the broker computed when it stored the message.

CamelRocketMQReconsumeTimes.label: consumer
CamelRocketMQReconsumeTimes.description: How many times RocketMQ has delivered the message again after a failed consumption, 0 on the first delivery.

CamelRocketMQPreparedTransactionOffset.label: consumer
CamelRocketMQPreparedTransactionOffset.description: For a message of a transaction, the commit log offset of its prepared (half) message.

consumerOut.description: The body of the RocketMQ message. The consumer does not reply: the body the route ends with is not sent back

producerIn.description: What converts to a byte array: text, bytes, a stream or a file, sent as the body of the message. A Map, a POJO, a number or no body fails, and the broker rejects an empty body: marshal it first

producerOut.description: The body is left as it was. With the InOut pattern and a replyToTopic, the producer waits for the reply and the body is the reply as a byte array

topicName.description: The name of the topic. The consumer subscribes to this topic, and the producer sends to it unless the CamelRocketMQOverrideTopicName header names another topic.
